title: Workloads use TopologySpreadConstraints, which v1.8.4 mis-schedules

detection.reason: reads the flag the agent writes for every workload; which specific constraint configurations trigger the regression is not stated upstream, so every workload declaring one is a candidate

quote: Karpenter `v1.8.4` release contains a regression which may prevent Karpenter from scheduling pods with specific TopologySpreadConstraint configurations. Please do not upgrade to this version. For more details, see the following issue: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/karpenter/issues/2785
remediation: Do not land on v1.8.4 — go to a later 1.8 patch. The workloads named here declare TopologySpreadConstraints, and that release contains a regression which can leave their pods unscheduled.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,statefulset,daemonset -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.template.spec.topologySpreadConstraints // []) != []) | "\(.kind)/\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each workload printed is exposed to the v1.8.4 scheduling regression

title: Static Capacity needs the Karpenter CRDs re-applied

detection.reason: the CRD's schema fields are not collected — only each CRD's name, group and served version names are

quote: This version adds support for Static Capacity. Make sure to upgrade your karpenter CRDs to use this feature.
remediation: Re-apply the Karpenter CRDs if you intend to use Static Capacity. Helm never updates CRDs on an upgrade, so on an un-updated CRD the API server strips the new fields from anything you write.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group | test("karpenter")) | "\(.metadata.name) served=\([.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] | join(","))"'  # each Karpenter CRD and the API versions it still serves
